The '''34th Academy Awards''', honoring the best in [[1961 in film|film for 1961]], were held on April 9, 1962, hosted by [[Bob Hope]] at the [[Santa Monica Civic Auditorium]] in [[Santa Monica, California]].

[[Robert Wise]] and [[Jerome Robbins]] became the first [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] co-winners for ''[[West Side Story (1961 film)|West Side Story]]''. The film won 10 of its 11 nominations, including [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] and both supporting acting Oscars, becoming the most successful musical in Oscars history. For the second time in history, all four acting winners were first-time nominees.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Collins |first1=Keith |title=Oscar facts & figures |url=https://variety.com/2006/film/awards/oscar-facts-figures-1117918228/ |access-date=June 15, 2026 |work=Variety |date=February 21, 2006 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190605184741/https://variety.com/2006/film/awards/oscar-facts-figures-1117918228/ |archive-date=June 5, 2019 }}</ref>

Legendary filmmaker [[Federico Fellini]] received his first [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] nomination for ''[[La Dolce Vita]]'', while [[Sophia Loren]] became the [[List of Italian Academy Award winners and nominees#Best Actress in a Leading Role|first Italian actress to win for Best Actress in an Italian-language film]] as well as the [[List of actors nominated for Academy Awards for non-English performances|first individual to win for a foreign-language performance]].<ref name="Rules">{{cite web |title=Special Rules for the Best Foreign Language Film Award |url=http://www.oscars.org/79academyawards/rules/rule14.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080314002549/http://www.oscars.org/79academyawards/rules/rule14.html |archive-date=2008-03-14 |access-date=2008-07-25 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]]}}</ref> Directors [[Robert Wise]] and [[Jerome Robbins]] became the first pair to share an Oscar for the same film.<ref name="Oscars '61 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/842/mode/2up |title=The People's Almanac |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |isbn=0-385-04060-1 |location=Garden City, New York |page=842|author-link=David Wallechinsky|author-link2=Irving Wallace}}</ref> [[George C. Scott]] became the first actor to refuse an award in advance, insisting that the [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor|Best Supporting Actor]] nomination for his performance in ''[[The Hustler]]'' be revoked. It was not, and he lost.<ref name="Oscars '61 Notes"/>

The most memorable event of the night came when Stan Berman, a New York City cabdriver famous for crashing celebrity parties, evaded security and made his way onstage to award Hope a homemade Oscar.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/03/awards-insider-oscars-gatecrasher-1962 | title=How "the World's Greatest Gate-Crasher" Made It to the Oscar Stage 60 Years Ago | website=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]] | date=March 23, 2022 }}</ref>

===Honorary Awards===
* To [[William L. Hendricks]] for his outstanding patriotic service in the conception, writing and production of the Marine Corps film, ''A Force in Readiness'', which has brought honor to the Academy and the motion picture industry.
* To Fred L. Metzler for his dedication and outstanding service to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.
* To [[Jerome Robbins]] for his brilliant achievements in the art of choreography on film.

===Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award===
* [[George Seaton]]

===Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award===
* [[Stanley Kramer]]
